docs.title: 17. Conclusion
docs.text:
The Creator 5 Pro is not a hopelessly closed system. It already contains Klipper, a clear Linux and data partition layout, serial Klipper MCUs, and an analyzable, non-stripped vendor application. Those properties make a staged opening substantially more realistic than on a printer with an entirely proprietary motion stack.

The hardest part is not Mainsail. It is the boundary between firmwareExe, MCU bootstrap, vendor Klipper extensions, and physical safety. Once runtime traces and heater-disabled tests document that boundary, the remaining work can be divided into controlled work packages.

The recommended order is therefore:

  1. Complete recovery.
  2. Observe firmwareExe and specify its interfaces.
  3. Start vendor Klipper without firmwareExe, but also without heaters or motion.
  4. Make Moonraker and Mainsail the sole operator and file-control path.
  5. Move functions individually into macros, Klipper modules, and Linux services.
  6. Build a clean rootfs only after the service graph is proven.
  7. Treat the kernel and bootloader as a separate, later BSP project.

This approach produces more than a working mod. It creates an auditable platform in which no single hidden binary or shell script controls the entire printer.

docs.title: FPV Gate Padding: Current Experience
docs.text: Note: This is not a scientific comparison. It reflects our current experience from building and operating FPV racing gates.

docs.title: Current favorite
docs.text:
Multiple layers of roll-stock PE foam covered with PVC truck-tarpaulin fabric

This combination currently offers the best balance of:

  • low cost
  • easy sourcing and cutting
  • adjustable thickness by adding or removing layers
  • adaptability to different gate shapes
  • a durable, repairable outer skin

At present, approximately 30–40 mm of total padding seems like a sensible target.

docs.title: PE foam from a roll
docs.text: We use a PE foam roll approximately 8 mm thick. Rolls around 10 mm thick should work just as well.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• very affordable
  • quick to cut into suitable strips
  • several layers make it easy to achieve the desired thickness
  • considerably cheaper than thick sheets or specialist foams

docs.title: Disadvantages and experience
docs.text:
Our PE foam performs extremely poorly under prolonged UV exposure. Unprotected areas became so porous that a single propeller touch broke the foam into fine plastic confetti. This creates a correspondingly large amount of plastic waste on the field.

Recommendation: Cover PE foam as completely and light-tight as possible. Based on our experience so far, inexpensive PE foam should not be assumed to have adequate UV resistance.

docs.title: PVC truck tarpaulin as the outer skin
docs.text: PVC truck-tarpaulin fabric has worked very well for us as the protective cover.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• durable and abrasion-resistant
  • waterproof
  • protects the foam from UV radiation
  • comparatively inexpensive
  • offcuts can sometimes be sourced cheaply from tarpaulin manufacturers
  • can be heat-welded
  • damage can be repaired easily with welded patches

docs.title: Disadvantages and experience
docs.text:
• it takes some practice to process cleanly
  • too much heat can damage the tarpaulin or the foam underneath
  • the cover should not be unnecessarily tight, so the foam can still absorb impacts

A hot-air gun, a suitable welding nozzle and a silicone pressure roller work well for welding. This normally makes adhesive unnecessary.

docs.title: Hot air and PE foam
docs.text:
PE foam can be carefully softened and shaped with hot air.

This can be useful for:

  • clean ends
  • compressed transitions
  • lightly fixing individual areas in place

The temperature window is narrow. A little too much heat causes the foam to collapse quickly. Always test on offcuts first.

docs.title: Thick PE/LDPE sheets
docs.text: Ready-made sheets approximately 30–40 mm thick are an alternative.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• consistent padding thickness
  • little assembly work
  • clearly defined construction

docs.title: Disadvantages
docs.text:
• considerably more expensive than thin roll stock
  • large sheets are expensive or difficult to ship
  • less flexible for different gate shapes

For now, multiple layers of PE roll foam therefore seem more attractive to us.

docs.title: EVA and cross-linked PE foam
docs.text: These are technically higher-quality alternatives with good impact absorption and durability.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• good mechanical properties
  • in some cases, better ageing and recovery characteristics

docs.title: Disadvantages
docs.text:
• considerably more expensive
  • so far, no clear benefit for an FPV gate that justifies the additional cost

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• soft
  • good damping
  • sometimes available at low cost

docs.title: Disadvantages
docs.text:
• less attractive for permanent outdoor use
  • moisture trapped under the cover can become a problem
  • mechanically less robust than PE-based solutions

docs.title: Pipe insulation
docs.text: We already have good long-term experience with pipe insulation.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• some products are highly weather- and age-resistant
  • easy to install when the dimensions are suitable
  • in our previous products, damaged areas tended to tear out in larger pieces instead of disintegrating into fine plastic confetti

docs.title: Disadvantages
docs.text:
• large diameters and thick walls become expensive quickly
  • suitable sizes for larger gate structures are difficult to find
  • this makes a complete cube less attractive on price

Pipe insulation nevertheless remains interesting for smaller elements or special areas.

docs.title: Current recommendation
docs.text:
For a cost-conscious rebuild, we would currently start with this system:

8–10 mm PE foam roll

→ multiple layers up to approximately 30–40 mm of padding

→ completely enclose it in opaque PVC truck-tarpaulin fabric

→ heat-weld the tarpaulin

For us, this is currently the best compromise between:

  • price
  • impact protection
  • availability
  • adaptability
  • repairability

docs.title: Key lessons
docs.text:
• Plan for sufficient thickness: Approximately 30–40 mm currently seems more useful than very thin padding.
  • Protect PE foam from UV: Exposed areas can become extremely brittle and produce plastic confetti.
  • The outer skin is critical: PVC tarpaulin protects the foam and takes the actual abrasion.
  • Design for repairability: PVC patches can be welded on quickly.
  • Do not automatically buy the most expensive foam: Specialist materials may perform better, but the benefit may not justify the price for an FPV gate.
  • Test before buying in volume: PE foams that look similar can differ substantially in hardness and durability.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Our current favorite is inexpensive PE roll foam in multiple layers, fully enclosed by heat-welded PVC truck-tarpaulin fabric.

The construction is affordable, flexible and easy to repair. Based on our experience so far, the decisive weakness of inexpensive PE foam is its UV sensitivity. Foam should therefore never be left permanently exposed.

docs.title: Capacitor for FPV Racing
docs.text: A good capacitor is still an important part of a reliable 5-inch FPV racing quad. If motors become unusually hot, the video system shows noise, the flight controller resets, or the quad suddenly feels inconsistent, a damaged, missing, or undersized ESC capacitor is worth checking. It is not a cure-all, but replacing it with a good low-ESR hybrid capacitor often helps.

docs.title: Recommended capacitors
docs.text:
For a normal 6S ESC with a radial, through-hole capacitor, these are the strongest choices from the comparison:

  1. Panasonic EEH-AZSV681UB — best practical first choice.
  2. KEMET A7C3MW687M1VAAS011 — closest technical replacement.
  3. Rubycon 35PZK680M10X15 — excellent electrical alternative, but usually harder to source.

For a custom PCB, the Panasonic EEH-ZU1V681UV has the best electrical values. The TDK/EPCOS B40950A7687M000 is another good SMD option. SMD parts are not drop-in replacements for a capacitor mounted on an ESC with free wires.

* Prices are example distributor listings from the research snapshot, not fixed quotes. Stock, packaging, region, and quantity can change the price.

docs.title: 35 V and 680 µF
docs.text:
A fully charged 6S LiPo reaches 25.2 V. A 35 V capacitor leaves 9.8 V of nominal headroom, which is a sensible minimum for a compact 6S ESC capacitor. It is not guaranteed transient protection: long battery leads, poor connectors, high current, and ESC layout can create short voltage spikes. Never intentionally operate the capacitor above its voltage rating.

The 680 µF local reservoir supplies short current pulses and reduces voltage ripple at the ESC battery input. More capacitance can help, but wiring, solder joints, mounting position, and ESR are equally important.

docs.title: ESR: the useful meaning of “internal resistance”
docs.text:
The important value is usually ESR, or equivalent series resistance. A simple approximation is:

voltage ripple ≈ current ripple × ESR

Lower ESR normally means less ripple voltage and less heat inside the capacitor. The radial Panasonic, KEMET, and Rubycon parts are all specified at about 11 mΩ. The Panasonic SMD part is specified at 9 mΩ; the TDK part at 15 mΩ. These values are normally measured at 100 kHz and 20 °C and should only be compared under matching conditions. Wiring inductance also contributes to the real transient impedance.

docs.title: Why hybrid instead of full polymer?
docs.text:
Hybrid aluminum electrolytic capacitors combine conductive polymer with liquid electrolyte. The polymer helps provide low ESR and high ripple-current capability, while the liquid electrolyte remains part of the wound aluminum-electrolytic system. This gives a useful combination of low impedance, compact size, temperature capability, and electrolytic construction.

Hybrid does not mean surge-proof. The capacitor still has a 35 V maximum rating and must be protected from excessive voltage, heat, reverse polarity, and crash damage.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
• Solder the radial capacitor directly across the ESC battery input: positive to VBAT and the marked negative lead to ground.
  • Keep the connection short and low impedance.
  • Insulate and mechanically secure the capacitor so a crash cannot bend the leads into a short circuit.
  • A second capacitor in parallel can reduce effective ESR, but it cannot compensate for very long battery leads or poor solder joints.
  • For a custom SMD board, provide the correct footprint and mechanical strain relief. Do not attach an SMD can to long unsupported wires.

The technical comparison used manufacturer datasheets and product pages from Panasonic, KEMET/YAGEO, Rubycon, and TDK. Full solid-polymer capacitors were excluded from this hybrid-only selection.
